(d) OFF-FRAME CLOSURE - the only genuinely ambiguous part; all in-frame ink is clean. Five wires leave the TOP edge (inductor 0, x=183, x=231, x=283, V-AC 11) and five leave the BOTTOM edge (col A x=77, col B x=167, col C x=221, inductor 5's lower lead x=277, V-DC 10's lower lead x=365). The five top stubs are taken as one rail (n1): that is the only reading that leaves no terminal dangling. At the bottom, a SINGLE rail joining all five stubs was REJECTED: column C's stub is electrically rung4 and column B's stub is ground, so one common rail would make rung4 = 0, which shorts V-DC 10 (both terminals on '0') and shorts I-DC 9 - a Tier-1 fault, and per the protocol almost certainly the wrong reading of ink we cannot see. The adopted reading is: the ground rail below the crop catches column A, column B (with GND 12 hanging from it) and V-DC 10's lower lead, while column C's tail and inductor 5's lower lead - the two adjacent stubs at x=221 and x=277 - join each other just below the frame and are therefore part of rung4 (n4). This leaves no dangling terminal, no shorted source, and a DC path to ground from every node. It does require one off-frame crossing (the ground rail passing under the col-C/inductor-5 link); every alternative closure either dangles a wire end or shorts a source.
